clauses.current_legal_basis: Held U.S. Code notes to 10 U.S.C. 1784 print section 568(d) of Pub. L. 104-106 (Feb. 10, 1996) making EO 12568 apply as if its reference to section 806(a)(2) of the 1986 Act referred to 10 U.S.C. 1784, print the order itself with no ending statement, and held current 10 U.S.C. 1784(a)(2) authorizes the same hiring preference; 3 U.S.C. 301 is held and in force. Bounded eCFR search as of 2026-10-14 and Federal Register disposition-note search found no revocation or amendment.
clauses.reason: The paragraph empowers the Secretary of Defense and designated military department officials to give hiring preference in nonappropriated fund activities to qualified spouses of members of the Armed Forces stationed in the same area, for wage grade UA-8 and below, equivalent positions and hourly-rate positions. It has no expiry or condition, no held later order revokes or amends it, Congress in 1996 expressly kept it in effect by pointing its statutory reference to 10 U.S.C. 1784, and the Code prints it as current, so it was operative on 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
EO 12568 (Reagan, signed 1986-10-02, 51 FR 35497, published 1986-10-06) empowers the Secretary of Defense and, as designated by him, the Secretaries, Under Secretaries and Assistant Secretaries of the Military Departments to exercise the discretionary authority granted to the President by subsection 806(a)(2) of the Department of Defense Authorization Act of 1986 (Public Law 99-145) to give hiring preference in nonappropriated fund activities to qualified spouses of members of the Armed Forces stationed in the same area, for positions in wage grade UA-8 and below, equivalent positions and positions paid at hourly rates. The authority statute was replaced rather than repealed: section 568(d) of Pub. L. 104-106 (February 10, 1996), printed in the held U.S. Code notes to 10 U.S.C. 1784, provides that the order applies as if its reference to section 806(a)(2) referred to section 1784 of title 10, and the held current text of 10 U.S.C. 1784(a)(2) carries the same preference authority. The order also cites 3 U.S.C. 301, which is held and in force. The Code prints the order as a note with no ending statement; the Federal Register disposition notes list no amendment or revocation.

savings.reason: The order is a continuing delegation with no end; Congress in 1996 directed that it apply as if it referred to 10 U.S.C. 1784, and no later instrument ending it was found, so no residual exists beyond the operative clause.
